description: Workflow Event History page -- the central observability hub for the Inngest-inspired workflow orchestration system. Displays a live-updating table of all workflow lifecycle events (completed, failed, started, step completed, verification passed/failed), a durable queue status dashboard showing pending/running/max-concurrent/max-depth with persistence indicator, a circuit breaker health widget showing open/closed/half-open state with failure count vs threshold, and active event subscriptions registered by the trigger system. Events are emitted by the Rust event bus (workflow_event_bus.rs) at task lifecycle transitions and consumed by the trigger_system for reactive WorkflowChain triggers. The page polls the MCP API endpoints GET /inngest/events, /inngest/subscriptions, /inngest/queue, and /inngest/circuit-breaker. Backend: mcp/inngest.rs (5 endpoints), workflow_event_bus.rs (pub/sub), database/queue_ops.rs (durable persistence), orchestrator/retry.rs (CircuitBreaker).

groups.name: Page Header and Identity
groups.description: The page header establishes the Workflow Event History identity with a Radio icon, shows aggregate counts (event count, subscription count), and auto-refreshes data every 5 seconds.

assertions.description: The page clearly identifies itself as Workflow Event History so users know this is the observability hub for workflow lifecycle events
The header shows the total number of events currently loaded, giving users a quick sense of activity volume
assertions.expected: A number followed by 'event' or 'events'

assertions.description: The header shows the number of active event subscriptions, indicating how many workflow chain triggers are listening
assertions.expected: A number followed by 'subscription' or 'subscriptions'

groups.name: Event Filtering
groups.description: A search/filter bar allows users to narrow down events by name pattern or source workflow. Essential when the event history is busy during multi-workflow orchestration.

assertions.description: A search input exists for filtering events
The filter input has descriptive placeholder text indicating what can be filtered

criteria.textContent: Filter by event name or source

assertions.description: Typing in the filter input immediately narrows the event table to only matching rows without requiring a submit action

target.label: Filter input with live filtering behavior

assertions.expected: Typing a string filters the table rows client-side in real time, matching against event name and source label

assertions.description: When the filter matches no events, a message indicates no results rather than showing an empty table
assertions.expected: Displayed when filter text produces zero matching events
assertions.precondition: At least one event exists but the filter excludes all of them

groups.name: Durable Queue Status Dashboard
groups.description: Compact widget displaying real-time state of the durable workflow queue. Data from GET /inngest/queue reflecting WorkflowQueue semaphore state and crash-recovery status. Backend: workflow_queue.rs, database/queue_ops.rs (SQLite + PG), main.rs (startup recovery).

assertions.description: Users can see how many workflows are waiting in the queue (pending count), indicating backlog pressure
Users can see how many workflows are currently executing (semaphore permits in use)
Maximum concurrent workflow limit is displayed for capacity understanding
Maximum queue depth is displayed, indicating the threshold beyond which new submissions are rejected
A colored dot (green=durable, gray=in-memory) indicates whether the queue persists to SQLite, surviving crashes
Queue counts (pending, running, max concurrent, max depth) display as numeric values with tabular-nums font for alignment
assertions.expected: Each stat widget shows a label followed by a bold numeric value

assertions.description: Queue status auto-refreshes every 5 seconds to reflect changes from workflow submissions and completions
assertions.expected: Queue widget polls GET /inngest/queue every 5000ms via useRunnerQuery

groups.name: Circuit Breaker Health Widget
groups.description: Displays state of the global circuit breaker (orchestrator/retry.rs). Shows: state (Closed=green, Open=red, Half-Open=yellow), failure count vs threshold, cooldown. When Open, all retries are rejected. After cooldown, a probe request is allowed (Half-Open). Backend: CircuitBreaker in AppState, queried via GET /inngest/circuit-breaker from mcp/inngest.rs.

assertions.description: The circuit breaker state is displayed as a labeled value (Closed, Open, or Half-Open)
The circuit state has a color-coded dot: green for Closed (healthy), red for Open (tripped), yellow for Half-Open (testing recovery)
assertions.expected: A 2x2 rounded-full dot element adjacent to the state label, class includes bg-green-500 (Closed), bg-red-500 (Open), or bg-yellow-500 (Half-Open)

assertions.description: Failure count is displayed as 'N / threshold' format showing proximity to tripping
Cooldown duration displayed in seconds so users know how long the circuit stays open
Circuit breaker state displayed matches the actual CircuitBreaker.state() in orchestrator/retry.rs â€” not a cached or stale value
assertions.expected: The displayed state reflects the live CircuitBreaker state via GET /inngest/circuit-breaker, polling every 5s. After 5 consecutive failures trip the breaker, the widget should show 'Open' within 5 seconds

groups.name: Event History Table
groups.description: Reverse-chronological table of workflow events. Each row: timestamp, color-coded event name, source workflow, truncated data preview. Rows are expandable to show full JSON payload and metadata. Events emitted by workflow_event_bus.rs at lifecycle transitions in task_lifecycle.rs.

assertions.description: Timestamp column header present for chronological orientation
Event Name column header for identifying what happened
Source column header for identifying which workflow produced the event
Data Preview column header for showing truncated event payload
Event names are color-coded by type: green for completed/success, red for failed/error, blue for started, yellow for step events, gray for others
assertions.expected: Event name text has class text-green-400 for completed events, text-red-400 for failed events, text-foreground for others

assertions.description: Each event row has a small colored dot indicator matching its event type for quick visual scanning
assertions.expected: A 2x2 rounded-full dot with class bg-green-500 (completed), bg-red-500 (failed), bg-blue-500 (started), bg-yellow-500 (step), or bg-zinc-500 (other)

assertions.description: Events are displayed newest-first (reverse chronological) so users see the most recent activity at the top
assertions.expected: The first table row has a more recent timestamp than the last row. Events returned by GET /inngest/events are reversed before display

assertions.description: Event data payloads are truncated to ~120 characters in the table with an ellipsis, preventing wide rows from breaking the layout
assertions.expected: Data preview cells show at most 120 characters followed by 'â€¦' if truncated. Full payload is visible in the expanded detail panel

assertions.description: Clicking an event row toggles an inline detail panel below it, showing full JSON payload, source metadata, and idempotency key
assertions.expected: On click, a detail panel (colSpan=4) appears below the row with: Full Payload (formatted JSON), Source details (task_run_id, workflow_id, workflow_name), idempotency key, and full timestamp. Clicking again collapses it

assertions.description: The expanded detail panel shows the full JSON payload formatted with 2-space indentation in a pre/code block

target.label: Full Payload label in detail panel

assertions.precondition: An event row has been clicked/expanded

assertions.description: The expanded detail panel shows source metadata including task_run_id, workflow_id, and workflow_name

target.label: Task Run ID in detail panel

assertions.precondition: An event row has been clicked/expanded

assertions.description: Event rows highlight on hover with a subtle background change for visual feedback
assertions.expected: Table rows have class hover:bg-muted/60 transition-colors for smooth hover feedback

groups.name: Active Subscriptions Panel
groups.description: Grid of active event subscriptions below the event table. Each card shows event pattern (monospace), green active dot, and 'once' badge. Subscriptions registered by trigger_system for WorkflowChain triggers. Polls GET /inngest/subscriptions every 15 seconds.

assertions.description: The subscriptions section has a clear heading
Subscription event patterns are displayed in monospace font for code readability

target.label: Monospace event pattern in subscription card

assertions.expected: Pattern text has class font-mono text-xs
assertions.precondition: At least one subscription is registered

assertions.description: Each subscription card has a green dot indicating it is actively listening

target.label: Green active dot on subscription card

assertions.expected: A 2x2 rounded-full dot with class bg-green-500 on each subscription card
assertions.precondition: At least one subscription is registered

assertions.description: Fire-once subscriptions are marked with a 'once' text badge to distinguish them from persistent subscriptions
assertions.expected: Displayed only on subscriptions where once=true, positioned at ml-auto
assertions.precondition: At least one fire-once subscription is registered

assertions.description: Subscription cards use a responsive grid layout that adapts from 1 column on mobile to 3 columns on desktop
assertions.expected: Container has classes grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3

groups.name: Empty, Loading, and Error States
groups.description: The page handles edge cases: offline runner (yellow warning), API errors (red banner), loading (spinner message), empty history (centered icon + message). These ensure users always understand system state.

assertions.description: When the runner is not connected, a yellow warning banner tells the user to check if qontinui-runner is running
assertions.precondition: Runner is not running or unreachable

assertions.description: When the API returns an error, a red error banner is displayed with the error message
assertions.expected: Red-tinted banner (bg-red-500/10 border-red-500/30 text-red-400) with error message text
assertions.precondition: Runner is connected but API returns an error

assertions.description: While events are loading for the first time, a loading message is centered on the page
assertions.precondition: Page has just mounted and first API call is in flight

assertions.description: When no events exist, a centered empty state with a Radio icon and message is shown instead of a blank area
assertions.precondition: Runner is connected, API succeeds, but event history is empty

groups.name: Navigation and Page Access
groups.description: The Event History page is accessible from the main app navigation at /event-history. It should load independently without requiring other pages to be visited first.

assertions.description: The page is accessible at /event-history and loads without redirects or prerequisites
assertions.expected: Navigating to /event-history renders the EventHistoryPage component directly

groups.name: Auto-Refresh and Data Freshness
groups.description: All data auto-refreshes via polling through useRunnerQuery. Events + queue + circuit-breaker poll every 5s; subscriptions every 15s. Polling is deduplicated by shared API client.

assertions.description: Event history auto-refreshes every 5 seconds to reflect new events within seconds of emission
assertions.expected: useRunnerQuery('/inngest/events?limit=100', { pollInterval: 5000 }) is called, fetching new events every 5 seconds

assertions.description: Subscription list refreshes every 15 seconds (slower since subscriptions change infrequently)
assertions.expected: useRunnerQuery('/inngest/subscriptions', { pollInterval: 15000 }) is called

assertions.description: Queue status, circuit breaker state, and event list are all from the same polling cycle, showing consistent system state
assertions.expected: All three widgets poll at the same 5s interval. While they're independent requests, the useRunnerQuery hook ensures near-simultaneous updates so queue 'Running: 1' and a recent 'workflow.started' event appear together

metadata.author: Joshua Spinak
dbTables: execution_spans (enriched v146: queue_wait_ms, retry_attempt, phase, iteration, workflow_id)

apiAssertions.description: Events endpoint returns success with array data
Queue endpoint returns all required fields with correct types
Circuit breaker endpoint returns state, failure count, threshold, cooldown
Circuit breaker is in closed (healthy) state on fresh start
Subscriptions endpoint returns success with array data
Flow control endpoint reports active status

states.name: Loading
states.description: Page has mounted and the initial API calls for events, queue, circuit breaker, and subscriptions are in flight. A centered loading message is displayed.

transitions.name: Data loaded successfully
transitions.description: All API calls return successfully and at least one event exists in the history

transitions.name: Data loaded but no events
transitions.description: API calls return successfully but event history is empty

transitions.name: Runner not reachable
transitions.description: The runner is not connected, triggering the offline warning banner

transitions.name: API error on load
transitions.description: Runner is connected but an API endpoint returns an error response

states.name: Runner Offline
states.description: The runner is not connected. A yellow warning banner tells the user to check if qontinui-runner is running. No data widgets are populated.

transitions.name: Runner reconnects
transitions.description: The runner comes back online and the page re-fetches data, returning to the loading state briefly

states.name: API Error
states.description: Runner is connected but one or more API endpoints returned an error. A red error banner is displayed with the error message.

transitions.name: Error clears on next poll
transitions.description: The next auto-refresh poll succeeds, clearing the error state and showing data

states.name: Empty History
states.description: Runner is connected and APIs succeed, but no workflow events have been recorded. A centered empty state with Radio icon and message is shown.

transitions.name: First event arrives
transitions.description: A workflow emits its first event and the next 5-second poll picks it up, populating the table

states.name: Populated View
states.description: The main operational state. Event table shows rows in reverse chronological order, queue status dashboard shows pending/running/max-concurrent/max-depth, circuit breaker widget shows state, and subscriptions panel shows active listeners. All widgets auto-refresh.

transitions.name: Apply event filter
transitions.description: User types in the filter input, narrowing the event table to matching rows in real time

transitions.name: Expand event row
transitions.description: User clicks an event row to reveal the inline detail panel with full JSON payload and metadata

states.name: Filtered View
states.description: The filter input has text and the event table is narrowed to rows matching the filter pattern against event name and source. Queue, circuit breaker, and subscriptions remain visible.

transitions.name: Clear filter
transitions.description: User clears the filter input, restoring the full unfiltered event table

transitions.name: Filter matches nothing
transitions.description: User types a filter string that does not match any events, showing a no-results message

transitions.name: Expand filtered event row
transitions.description: User clicks an event row in the filtered view to expand its detail panel

states.name: No Filter Results
states.description: The filter input has text but no events match the pattern. A message indicates no results rather than showing an empty table.

transitions.name: Adjust filter to match
transitions.description: User changes the filter text to a pattern that matches one or more events

transitions.name: Clear filter from no-match
transitions.description: User clears the filter input entirely, restoring the full event table

states.name: Event Row Expanded
states.description: An event row has been clicked and the inline detail panel is visible below it, showing the full JSON payload, source metadata (task_run_id, workflow_id, workflow_name), idempotency key, and full timestamp.

transitions.name: Collapse event row
transitions.description: User clicks the expanded row again to collapse the detail panel, returning to the previous view state
